subject: Marketplace revenue routing & audit path for partner paper
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudmarq.com>

Cc: CloudMarq Legal <legal@cloudmarq.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial partner-paper redline and questions on revenue routing

Hi Tessa,

Attaching our initial redline to the partner paper. Two items we want to confirm before formalizing:

1) Revenue routing: when the transaction originates through the marketplace, CloudMarq typically requires the partner (Redwood) to accept pass-through allocation so CloudMarq can reconcile end-customer billing in their system. We marked a clause in the Order Form to reflect a revenue assignment flow but would like your legal team to confirm the mechanics (who invoices whom, and whether any commissions remain payable if CloudMarq collects).

2) Audit & evidence: we ask for yearly audit rights limited to revenue allocation records and invoices for the last 24 months. Is Redwood able to provide those with reasonable redaction?

We also proposed a narrower indemnity for marketplace-related third-party connectors — see Section 7 notes.

Attachment: CloudMarq_PartnerPaper_v0_redline.pdf (pdf, 220 KB)

If you prefer, we can hop on a quick 30-min call next week to walk through the redline.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of Partnerships, CloudMarq
rajiv@cloudmarq.com

Subject: Re: Initial partner-paper redline and questions on revenue routing

Rajiv — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Looping Ben and Laura to own pricing & legal responses. Quick notes from my side:

- We understand CloudMarq's need to reconcile marketplace-originated transactions. Our standard approach is: marketplace collects gross and remits net to Redwood (after marketplace fee), or alternatively marketplace can remit gross and Redwood pays commission to CloudMarq. We need to pick one flow for the Order Form; both have different tax/audit implications.

- For audit rights: Redwood can provide invoices and payment traces for the last 24 months with PII redacted; for customer-facing documents we usually require an NDA addendum and a limited-scope audit clause (timeboxed, sample-based).

Ask: can you confirm whether CloudMarq requires a full pass-through (they invoice and collect) or an allocation-only approach where Redwood still invoices end-customers? That will determine whether we include a reseller-assignment or a gateway-pass-through clause.

I've attached a short summary we will share internally: RWD_Response_Summary.docx. Laura — can you please review the indemnity carve-out and propose language for the marketplace context? Ben — please confirm whether this deal keeps standard Redwood list prices or if there is a special marketplace seat revenue split we should track.

Happy to schedule a 30-min sync with legal to close this after we exchange redlines.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RWD_Response_Summary.docx (docx, 45 KB)

Subject: Re: Initial partner-paper redline and questions on revenue routing

Tessa / Rajiv — quick commercial note from Sales:

- Deal ID RDW-8421 targets Q3 pilot (50 seats). For velocity we prefer CloudMarq to handle customer billing (marketplace collects) and remit net to Redwood. Practically, CloudMarq would report gross ARR and remit the agreed net.

- Revenue split: propose CloudMarq receives 20% commission on marketplace-originated revenue; Redwood records revenue net of commission. This avoids double-billing and simplifies bookkeeping.

- SLA credits: if marketplace billing path introduces payment delays >30 days, we need a fallback where Redwood can invoice directly to preserve cashflow. Please flag if this is acceptable.

If CloudMarq can accept the remit-net model and the 20% commission, we can proceed with Laura's legal language.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudmarq.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood legal redline and proposed marketplace-specific clauses

Rajiv — attaching Redwood's redline with targeted edits for the marketplace scenario. Highlights:

- Revenue routing: we propose a "remit-net" Exhibit in the Order Form. Clause language clarifies that CloudMarq will remit net proceeds to Redwood within 45 days of collection and provide CSV reconciliation reports (invoice id, date, gross_amount, marketplace_fee, net_remitted).

- Audit: we will accept one annual limited-scope audit of revenue allocation records for the previous 24 months. Audit to be sample-based (max 10 orders) and performed remotely; Redwood may redact PII. Any additional audits require mutual written consent and cost allocation.

- Indemnity: Redwood requests narrowly tailored indemnity for third-party connectors related to marketplace plug-ins — liability limited to direct damages capped at the fees paid by CloudMarq in the prior 12 months, excluding punitive and consequential damages. We strike broad open-ended indemnities.

- Fallback billing: added a clause that gives Redwood the right to invoice end-customers directly if CloudMarq fails to remit net proceeds within 90 days of collection, after a 30-day cure period.

Please see attached: RWD_Legal_Redline_markups.pdf (pdf, 120 KB).

If this direction works, we'll produce a clean Order Form Exhibit for signature and draft a short NDA-addendum for audit access.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: RWD_Legal_Redline_markups.pdf (pdf, 120 KB)

From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@cloudmarq.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood legal redline and proposed marketplace-specific clauses

Laura / Tessa — appreciate the detailed response and the pragmatic approach. Quick confirmations:

- CloudMarq can operate remit-net and provide the CSV reconciliation as proposed. 45-day remittance is acceptable.
- The sample-based audit (10 orders, remote, redacted PII) is fine; we'll sign an NDA-addendum.
- Indemnity cap tied to prior 12 months fees is reasonable for a pilot.
- Fallback billing clause is acceptable; we request a 60-day cure window instead of 30 to allow operational reconciliation.

Next steps: Laura to issue a clean Exhibit with the agreed edits and Rajiv will review. After internal acceptance CloudMarq will circulate a DocuSign envelope for the Order Form + Exhibit. Can we target execution by close of week Jul 2?

Action items:
- Laura: produce clean Exhibit + NDA-addendum (RWD)
- Tessa/Ben: confirm commission % (Ben proposed 20%) and confirm pilot metrics
- Rajiv: will prepare DocuSign envelope once clean doc is provided

Thanks — Rajiv
Head of Partnerships, CloudMarq
